phase_name: Defect 5 — Gate 16's WARN finding stops escalating to batch-blocking

objectives.description: Change warn()'s FINDINGS_LIST appends to a severity-bearing prefix (e.g. WARN-FINDING)
Update warn()'s header comment with the severity convention rationale
Update Findings-mode header block protocol documentation
Confirm no change to extensions/lean/manifest.json (deliberate no-op)
Extend gate-findings test with severity assertions
Stage and commit with explicit pathspec

approaches_tried.approach: Apply WARN-FINDING prefix change directly inside shared warn()
approaches_tried.reason: A second warn() caller exists (gate20's per-file budget-ceiling check, ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE=warn) that an existing test (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) asserts stays on the plain FINDING channel for attributability. Blanket-applying the prefix would have silently broken that test and regressed gate20's attributability. Resolved by introducing a separate warn_advisory() function used only by gate16, leaving warn() (and gate20) untouched.

verification_notes.scope_hypothesis_correction: The plan's Scope Hypothesis asserted warn() has a single caller (gate16). grep -n 'warn ' verify-deploy.sh found a SECOND caller at gate20 (per-file budget-ceiling check, default ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE=warn). Per the plan's own contingency instruction, re-checked whether the prefix change was still correct for it: NOT directly, because test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's case1/case2 assert exactly 1 'FINDING gate20' line for a WARN-mode per-file-ceiling breach (intentional batch-attributability, distinct from gate16's unattributable, perpetually-recurring nudge). Resolved by splitting into a new warn_advisory() function (WARN-FINDING prefix) used only by gate16's call site, while warn() keeps its original FINDING-prefix behavior for gate20 and any future caller.
